generation_protocol: every row generated cold in its own process (one process per row and colour accuracy, generation in the timing process as before; g g > g g g g g in its storing process): fresh PYAMPLICOL_CACHE_DIR per job (the counterterm-IR/Weyl model caches are rebuilt in every run) and the harness's fresh compiled-model directory; stages model / generate (LoopSlice.generate) / export (NativeExecutor), each with its peak RSS after a reset (VmHWM), and plan_mb. The previous records (1d27426b and earlier) ran without PYAMPLICOL_CACHE_DIR, i.e. with the user's default model cache, whose counterterm-IR entries were already present (warm): paired A/B on one idle core (generate stage, s): u u~ > e- e+ g g LC 1d27426b cold 39.6 / warm 10.9 (its m1025a record 10.7), 11542fd5 cold 25.6 / warm 10.9; u u~ > d d~ g FC 1d27426b cold 8.8 / warm 6.0 (record 6.4), 11542fd5 cold 8.9 / warm 5.9. So the cold rebuild of the counterterm IR (3-15 s) explains every small row's longer generate stage; like for like the small rows are unchanged (warm) or faster (cold). The model stage (the harness's compile_loop_sm, the same for every row) peaks at 0.36-0.37 GiB instead of 0.19 and takes 4.3-4.9 s instead of 3.5-4.2: introduced by model-determinism (4e9262b5; bisected: 18ed6674 0.18 GiB, 4e9262b5 with its native staged 0.35 GiB, 11542fd5 0.35 GiB), which raises the peak RAM of the rows whose generation peak is below about 0.7 GiB by 0.1-0.2 GiB
